assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine formation, previously a harsh and narrow transformation, into a routine, general bond construction. It is used across pharmaceutical discovery, process chemistry and materials, and is a textbook example of ligand design enabling a hard step. It is the closest fit to the Nobel standard of a method that changed how chemists everywhere build bonds.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic amination, with successive ligand generations and mechanistic work; the Kosugi tin-amide precedent is earlier and more limited. A two-person prize is clean. I am drawing on memory for precedence details and have not verified them.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of independent use, industrial adoption at scale, and a settled mechanism. The 2010 cross-coupling prize covered C-C coupling, so recognition of C-N coupling is complementary but may be seen as partly redundant.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views C-N coupling as a distinct step beyond the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Allocation of credit to Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work versus the catalytic amine-based variants.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization lets chemists form bonds at unactivated C-H sites, shortening synthetic routes, which is the efficiency theme I care most about. Directing-group, ligand and template control extended it from curiosity to a planning tool in late-stage functionalization and total synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand- and template-enabled, including meta and distal C-H activation), Sanford (Pd(II)/Pd(IV) and oxidative functionalization) and Hartwig (borylation and related work) made distinct decisive advances. Daugulis and Smith also have strong claims, so any trio leaves out credible contributors; this is a compound discovery.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature with broad adoption in medicinal chemistry, though industrial use at scale is still uneven and selectivity and generality continue to evolve. Timing is plausible but the field has not fully settled.
uncertainties: Unresolved credit among Yu, Sanford, Hartwig, Daugulis and Smith.
Hartwig appears across multiple candidate areas, so combined recognition is uncertain.
Practical scale-up generality is still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and open-shell reactivity under mild conditions and has spread widely in discovery chemistry, including dual catalysis with nickel and organocatalysis. The conceptual novelty is a general way to generate radicals by single-electron transfer from excited photocatalysts.
assessment.attribution: The 2008 reports from MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson were the decisive modern launch, with Nicewicz, Konig, Fukuzumi and Melchiorre as important contributors; the field's precursors (Kellogg, Fukuzumi, Cano-Yelo and Deronzier) complicate credit. MacMillan is already a 2021 laureate for organocatalysis, which may weigh against.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted and independently confirmed, with industrial and flow applications. Recognition is not premature but the field is still evolving and the credit situation is diffuse.
uncertainties: MacMillan's prior Nobel Prize may affect committee willingness.
Precursor work blurs who first established the concept.
Large, diffuse community makes a three-person limit arbitrary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptide segments, giving access to synthetic proteins and semisynthetic proteins with site-specific modifications. It is conceptually simple, general and widely taken up, a genuine chemical advance in making large molecules.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson introduced native chemical ligation in 1994 with Muir, and Muir with Kent developed expressed protein ligation. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu extended the logic (desulfurization, glycoprotein synthesis, mirror-image proteins), so credit is shared but the founding trio is fairly clear.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with 30 years of use and independent adoption. Its impact is largely in chemical biology rather than industrial production, which a synthetic chemist would weigh somewhat modestly.
uncertainties: Whether the extension work by Danishefsky, Brik and Liu deserves recognition.
Breadth of impact beyond a specialist community.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new chemical modality, and degraders are in clinical trials. What was new chemically is the design of bifunctional molecules that induce proximity to an E3 ligase, a strong design concept, although the underlying chemistry is largely modular medicinal chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept in 2001, Ciulli contributed structure-based VHL ligands and ternary-complex rationale; Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Gray and others contributed through cereblon biology and glues. Credit is multi-part and a fair trio is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still emerging and no degrader has yet matured into a broadly proven drug class, so recognition may be a little early. Strongly timely in terms of impact and independent confirmation.
uncertainties: Cereblon and molecular glue work by Handa, Ito and others may need to be separated from PROTAC credit.
Border with biology: the chemistry may be judged incremental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically encumbered acid-base pairs activate H2 and other small molecules without metals, and enabled metal-free hydrogenation. It is a clear and original conceptual contribution to main-group chemistry, with a simple, teachable picture.
assessment.attribution: Stephan (2006 discovery of reversible H2 activation by phosphine-borane) and Erker (extensive follow-up and intramolecular systems) form a natural pair. I am reasonably confident of this but have not verified the chronology.
assessment.maturity: Well-confirmed conceptually and widely studied, but the practical impact on synthesis and industry is modest compared with transition-metal catalysis, so lasting influence is less proven.
uncertainties: Whether the novelty outweighs the more limited scope of applications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolable stable carbenes overturned the assumption that carbenes are fleeting, and N-heterocyclic carbenes became ubiquitous ligands (e.g. in olefin metathesis catalysts) and organocatalysts. Very important for how catalysts are built, with a clear conceptual leap.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand reported the first isolable phosphinocarbene in 1988, and Arduengo the first crystalline NHC in 1991, so both are decisive. Nolan, Rovis and Bode are important for ligand and organocatalytic applications but are less central to the original discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature and thoroughly confirmed with large downstream use. The metathesis prize in 2005 partly covered related catalyst use, which may reduce novelty.
uncertainties: Fair split between structural discovery and catalytic applications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry underlies automated oligonucleotide synthesis, enabling PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide drugs. Its practical impact is enormous and it is a robust, general synthetic method.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method in the early 1980s; Hood is credited for the automation instrument. As a method contribution, Caruthers alone is the most defensible choice, though Hood's role in the instrument could justify a pair; I am uncertain about precise attribution.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, over 40 years of use, so recognition is not premature, but the discovery is old and the long delay may mean the field considers it overlooked or already absorbed.
uncertainties: Whether Hood's automation role deserves joint recognition.
Possible earlier phosphite-triester work by Letsinger and others affects precedence.
